channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: This Tool Brings 2D Painting Workflows Into Unreal Engine 5
item.description: Inky recreates traditional painting materials inside Unreal Engine 5, letting artists paint 3D assets with a 2D workflow.

item.title: Sensor Tower introduces web store revenue estimates
item.description: Sensor Tower now estimates direct-to-consumer web store revenue, giving developers a fuller picture of app and game monetisation beyond the stores.

item.title: Flutter Flame Tutorial: Build Your First 2D Game (Beginner Guide)
item.description: If you already know Flutter, you're closer to shipping your first game than you think — this beginner guide walks you through building a 2D game with the Flame engine.

item.title: Mastering Steamworks: A Technical Guide for Indie Publishing
item.description: A hands-on technical guide that breaks down the Steamworks APIs and tools to help indie developers get publishing, player experience and discoverability right.

item.title: Learn the Art of Making AAA Game-Ready Characters Using Industry-Standard Tools
item.description: This Wingfox master class walks through the complete workflow of creating game-ready characters, aimed at artists who want to reach AAA quality.

item.title: Game Engines Were World Models All Along
item.description: The final part of this series argues that a game loop is already a world model — state, action, next state, render — and that game developers have been building the foundations of AI world models all along.

item.title: Player Data Privacy Considerations For LLM-Driven In-Game NPCs
item.description: Open-dialogue NPCs accept freeform player text, and once that flows to external LLM services with logging and cross-region transfer, privacy compliance risks need mapping out before the feature goes live.

item.title: Unreal Engine 6 won't include Blueprints or Actor Gameplay Framework
item.description: Epic confirms Unreal Engine 6 will drop Blueprints and the Actor Gameplay Framework in favor of Verse and the new Scene Graph framework, marking a major shift in engine workflow.

item.title: Data digest: Monopoly Go hits $8bn, Block Blast and Vita Mahjong lead ad charts, Korea stats, more
Creating Game-Ready Fictional Military Vehicle In 3D
item.description: The artist walks through the workflow behind the original XM-118 Onza 8x8 fire support vehicle, from detailed interiors and a detachable turret to a fully drivable Unreal Engine setup.

item.title: Which Is the Best Game Engine: Unity, Unreal, or Godot?
item.description: There is no universal best engine, only the best fit for a given team size and production shape, and the author compares Unity, Unreal and Godot across scenarios from a two-person mobile team to a 20-person systems-heavy crew.

item.title: Is your data telling you the whole story?
item.description: Fragmented data hides the full player picture — this post explains what it costs UA and monetization teams and how to connect MMP, GA and IAP signals to Unity Vector.

item.title: Recreating the Atmosphere of a Middle Eastern Market in Unreal Engine 5 with Nuanced Lighting
item.description: Wendao shares what he learned from a new approach to lighting, explaining how he used color grading to make the scene atmospheric while keeping it realistic, and how he handled the lighting work.

item.title: Recreating the Atmosphere of a Middle Eastern Market in Unreal Engine 5
item.description: Wendao shares what he learned from a new approach to lighting, explaining how he used color grading to make the scene atmospheric while keeping it realistic, and how he handled the lighting work.

item.title: Choosing a Game Engine Before You Hire: A Decision Sheet for Funded Founders in India
item.description: Newly funded game startups in India often post job ads for a "Unity developer" or "Unreal developer" within a week of closing a round, only to discover later that the engine doesn't fit the project — this piece offers a decision sheet for choosing before you hire.

item.title: How To Model & Texture PS1-Style Character In Blender
item.description: Creator TomGrave3D walks through the design choices and full workflow behind a PS1-style character in Blender.

item.title: Godot 4 tileset terrains tutorial: paint paths and ponds that place their own corners
item.description: Godot 4's terrain system paints paths and ponds that place their own corners, so you can stop hand-placing every edge tile.

item.title: Godot 4 web export for itch.io: the settings that stop failed to fetch
item.description: Your Godot 4 web export fails to fetch on itch.io because a file is missing or thread support is misconfigured — this walkthrough checks every setting.

item.title: Gram Engine - Interlude 1.5: Gram Build on Three Platforms
item.description: The author set up Debug, Release and Final build modes to run a homebrew ray-tracing engine on three platforms, and tripped over Xcode failing to find Cargo along the way.

item.title: Pixel art effects with AI agents: our tool against pixelfx in four blind-judged blocks, losses first
item.description: The Pixelbolt team had Claude agents generate 16 pixel-art effects with its own tool and the open-source pixelfx, scored them in blind judging, and reports its losses first, giving indie developers a scoring approach to judge whether AI-made game effects are good enough to ship.
